title: Introduce KMS-Usage-Enforcer and Audit-Orphan-Cleaner for tenant residency enforcement
author: Anjali Rao
release_notes: Add KMS usage enforcement policy for tenant region pinning; background audit orphan cleaner to remove stale audit entries referencing retired CMKs; add RBAC v2 delegation guard for cross-region operator roles; non-disruptive rollout with feature flag and canary window
commits: a1f3b2f Add KMS usage enforcer policy and basic validation rules
b4d2c9e Implement audit orphan cleaner background worker
c3e9d11 Add RBAC v2 delegation guard and unit tests
d5f6b7a Update docs and rollout notes; add canary feature flag support
body:
Motivation: Several customers requested stricter enforcement that CMKs used for encrypting tenant data must be region-aligned with the tenant's residency setting. Previously we relied on best-effort checks in the private installer and operator docs; this PR introduces a policy + runtime guard to validate KMS claims at enforcement points and a background auditor to remove or flag audit records that reference retired or out-of-scope keys.

This PR includes: (1) policies/kms-usage-enforcer.yaml — an RBACv2 policy fragment that defines a kube-like admission-style guard for KMS claims: it validates the key's region attribute against tenant.residency and rejects requests where the key is outside the allowed zone unless the operator role is explicitly delegated and timebound; (2) policies/rbac-delegation-guard.yaml — a small policy that restricts cross-region operator delegation to short TTLs and requires an approval annotation; (3) tools/audit-cleaner — a small background worker (Go) that scans the audit ledger for entries pointing to KMS key ARNs in retired zones and either tags them as orphaned or prunes them after an admin retention window.

Design notes: We intentionally keep enforcement opt-in behind the feature flag "kms_residency_enforcement" so that Dedicated and Private customers can enable during a maintenance window. The enforcer runs synchronously at the final admission point for encryption requests (hosted path: encryption proxy; private path: installer hooks). When the policy would reject, the response surface returns a 403 with an error code X-KMS-REGION-MISMATCH and a remediation hint linking to the admin docs. For operator flows that require cross-region key use we support a delegation annotation (rbac.redwood.io/delegate-region) that must be accompanied by an operator-approved ticket id (Linear/Jira) and is limited to 4 hours by default.

Audit cleaner behavior: The cleaner uses the same residency rules to identify audit records that reference keys which are no longer in-scope (rotated/retired/region-changed). It writes a new audit tag "kms_orphaned: true" and increments a metric audit_orphan_count; after 30 days (configurable) orphaned records are pruned to satisfy retention and reduce exposure surface. Pruned entries are recorded in a tamper-evident prune log stored separately.

Testing: Unit tests added for policy rule edge cases (missing residency attribute, ambiguous region tags). Integration tests exercise a canary flow where enforcement is enabled for a single tenant and we assert the blocking and delegation paths. Local run: make test-integration passes, CI shows build/test/lint green after small lint fix to audit-cleaner imports.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag off. 2) Deploy audit-cleaner to staging and enable canary tenant via feature flag. 3) Monitor metrics: kms_enforcer_rejects, audit_orphan_count, rbac_delegation_grants. 4) If stable for 72h, toggle feature on for additional tenants in waves. We include a rollback script to disable the feature flag and re-run a pass that converts reject responses into warnings for 24h.

Security review: Reviewed by security and SRE (Michael Chen, Sofie Alvarez). We added rate limiting on the enforcer path to avoid amplification attacks and bounded the audit-cleaner worker concurrency. Key validation uses existing KMS metadata API with cached TTL to avoid per-request KMS calls.

Backward compatibility: When disabled, no behavior changes. Feature flag on may cause new 403 responses — documented in docs/security/kms-residency.md.

Related: ENG-4142 (residency policy backlog), SEC-88 (compliance remediation for EU tenant controls).

Checklist: - [x] Policy YAML and unit tests - [x] Enforcer implementation stubbed in admission point - [x] Background audit-cleaner and Dockerfile - [x] Integration tests for canary path - [x] Docs and rollout notes - [x] Security review sign-off

Manual steps for operators (high level): 1) Ensure feature flag is present in config and disabled by default. 2) Deploy audit-cleaner with k8s CronJob schedule or sidecar in Private installer. 3) For exceptional cross-region keys, create a delegation entry with a Linear ticket and set annotation rbac.redwood.io/delegate-region: <ticket>. 4) Monitor audit_orphan_count and run admin prune job if needed.

This PR is intentionally scoped to policy + tooling; it does not attempt to modify model-serving code paths directly — we will follow up with adapters in the encryption proxy and private installer to call the enforcer at the canonical point of encryption key selection.
review_comments: Michael Chen: Looks good overall; please add a small circuit-breaker metric for the enforcer path so SRE can kill it quickly if we see a spike.
Anjali Rao: Added enforcer_circuit_breaker metric and patched the worker to respect it. Pushed commit b4d2c9e.
Sofie Alvarez: Can we narrow the default delegation TTL to 2 hours instead of 4? Risk of long-lived cross-region keys concerns me.
Anjali Rao: Updated default to 2h in rbac-delegation-guard.yaml and noted it in the docs. Pushed commit c3e9d11.
Ravi Patel: Integration tests flaked once on CI due to DB connection limits — increased concurrency cap to 3 and re-ran.
Michael Chen: Approved after seeing metrics and docs; requested a follow-up to add telemetry dashboards.
additional_notes: CI initially failed lint on tools/audit-cleaner imports; fixed in second commit.
